detail: Row 259's remaining third: the date strings the register carries that a parser cannot read as a plain date. Every born, died and fact date on all 149 published people, read on 22 September 2026. 215 distinct date strings, 157 of them not in a plain "D Month YYYY" form.

finding: *** THE ROW SAID FIFTY-TWO UNPARSED STRINGS AND THE REAL NUMBER IS THIRTY-ONE, AND NONE OF THEM IS UNPARSED ***
detail: Every single date string in the register yields a year to year(). Not one fails. The fifty-two was a count of strings that are not in the canonical format, and most of those are simply "Aug 8 1884" — a different shape, not a harder one. THE REAL POPULATION IS THIRTY-ONE STRINGS THAT CARRY A QUALIFIER, and the danger was never that they could not be parsed. IT IS THAT THEY PARSE TOO WELL.

finding: *** THE FAULT: year() RETURNS A BARE INTEGER AND THROWS THE QUALIFIER AWAY ***
detail: year() takes the FIRST four-digit year in the string. bloodline.astro printed that integer and timeline.astro PLOTTED A POINT AT IT. So "Before 1955" arrived as 1955 and was published as a death in 1955; "After May 13 1942" arrived as 1942 and was published as a death in 1942. A BOUND WAS BEING PRINTED AS A DATE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE REGISTER COULD NOT TELL YOU WHICH ENTRIES THOSE WERE because the qualifying word was discarded at parse time.

FOUR. Twenty-seven of the thirty-one are on FACTS, which are rendered as the source text and so carry their own qualifier onto the page intact. Only born and died feed the derived `by`/`dy`, and those are what /bloodline/ prints and /timeline/ plots. *** JOACHIM LUWINSKI, died "Before 1955" — published as 1955. ELLI LEIBHOLZ (STRUZIK), died "After May 13 1942" — published as 1942. JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT, born "Circa 1923" — published as 1923. MARIA ELIZABETH VAN STRAATEN (OELOFSE), born "Circa Jan 1876" — published as 1876. ***

finding: THE FIX IS IN THE BUILDER, NOT THE DATA
detail: build-register.py now has qualifier(), which returns 'before', 'after', 'circa', 'range' or nothing, and every record carries `byq` and `dyq` beside `by` and `dy`. The correction loop sets them too, so a corrected date cannot re-introduce the fault — WHICH IS THE LESSON FROM THE KURT CASE FOUR HOURS EARLIER, where a correction reached `died` and never reached `dy`. Both pages now print the word: the bloodline reads "1865 – before 1955", and the timeline still has to plot a point somewhere but says in its own date column what kind of point it is.

finding: *** AND ONE OF THE FOUR COULD BE REPLACED OUTRIGHT, BY WORK DONE THE SAME DAY ***
detail: ELLI LEIBHOLZ, MARRIED STRUZIK, BORN 7 NOVEMBER 1915. The family record's "After May 13 1942" is not a guess — it is THE DEPORTATION DATE, the last day anybody knew she was alive, written down as the only honest thing that could be said. The fifty Gedenkbuch records loaded into this archive the same evening contain her: entry en1169257, Elli Struzik née Leibholz, born 07.11.1915 in Berlin, of Berlin (Mitte), Litzmannstadt 1 November 1941, KULMHOF 13 MAY 1942, died 00.05.1942 at Kulmhof. The birth date matches to the day. Correction 9500147 now carries her death as MAY 1942 AT KULMHOF. THE YEAR ON THE PAGE DOES NOT CHANGE, which is exactly the point worth recording: the archive was right by accident, because a floor and the truth fell in the same year. Joachim's "Before 1955" has no such luck behind it.

finding: THE OTHER TWENTY-SEVEN, AND WHY THEY ARE LEFT ALONE
detail: Ranges on facts, and some are wide: Michael Kurt Leibholz carries six, including "Between June 1 1981 and Dec 31 1989" and "From Dec 6 1993 To Nov 3 2005" — eight and twelve years. Siegfried Leibholz has "From Jan 1943 To Apr 30 1945" and "Circa Oct 24 1947". Johanna Thimm has "From Aug 2 1930 To July 23 1932". THESE ARE RESIDENCES AND OCCUPATIONS, not lives, and a range is the correct shape for them — a person really did live somewhere between two dates. They are printed as the source wrote them and no number is derived from them, so nothing is being asserted that the source does not say.

Johannes Antonie Oelofse de Witt's death is recorded as "2 April 1963, Sasolburg" — A PLACE INSIDE A DATE FIELD. year() reads 1963 correctly and nothing is wrong on the page, but a date field holding a town is the kind of thing that breaks the next parser somebody writes against it.

The third leg. This pass and the mechanical one before it both checked THE REGISTER AGAINST ITSELF. Not one date in prose has yet been reconciled to the document it came from, and that is the expensive part and the part where the Sauerbaum-distance kind of error lives.
